title: Fixed-point localization
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let $X$ be a
proper finite-type scheme.
Let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an
admissible
cohomological correspondence with
$c_2$ proper and with
fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ proper over $s$. For
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, the
categorical trace of the
global operator equals the integral of
the trace class:

$$
\operatorname{tr}_A\bigl(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K)\bigr)
=\int_F\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)
\quad\text{in }A,
$$

where $T_c(u)$ is the global operator of
[def-trf-global-operator], $\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ the trace class
of [def-trf-trace-class], and $\int_F$ the integration of
[def-trf-integration].

proof.text: Write $a_X:X\to s$, $a_C=a_Xc_2=a_Xc_1$ and $a_F:F\to s$. The composition clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] makes $a_C$ proper. Its base-change and composition clauses make $X\times_sX$ proper over $s$: its second projection is a base change of $a_X$, and its structure map is that projection followed by $a_X$. Thus $s,X,C,F,X\times_sX$ are all proper over $s$ (properness of $F$ is a hypothesis). For any $s$-morphism between these schemes, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] applies with its source structure map and its separated target, and makes that morphism proper. This covers the legs, total correspondence map, fixed-square maps, diagonals and structure maps needed below, and also the maps to the point correspondence. In particular the two projections $X\times_sX\to X$ are maps from the proper product to the separated scheme $X$, so are proper by the same cited statement; the projections of $s\times_ss$ are identities under its canonical identification with $s$. In particular they are separated finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Proof, opening paragraph and The pushforward to the point: properness of the source and all relevant maps

proof.text: At $Y=D=s$ take $b_1=b_2=\operatorname{id}_s$. With $f=a_X$ and $g=a_C$, both maps are proper by step 1 and $b_ig=a_C=a_Xc_i$ for $i=1,2$. These are exactly the conditions of [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward]. [def-trf-fixed-scheme] defines the fixed scheme as the scheme-theoretic inverse image of the diagonal, with its fibre-product projections and relation $c\circ i_F=\Delta_X\circ d$; its separated finite-type hypotheses hold by step 1. In particular this construction retains the scheme structure of the inverse image, including nilpotents. For $b$, this gives $F_b=s\times_{s\times_ss,b,\Delta_s}s$. Identify $s\times_ss$ with $s$; then $b$ and $\Delta_s$ are identities. The two projections $i_b,d_b:F_b\to s$ consequently agree. The universal property gives $e:s\to F_b$ with $i_be=d_be=\operatorname{id}_s$, and $ei_b=\operatorname{id}_{F_b}$ because both its projections equal those of the identity. Thus $d_b=i_b$ identifies $F_b$ with $s$. The fixed-map equations in [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] give $d_bh=a_Xd_c=a_F$, so under this identification the induced fixed map is precisely $h=a_F:F\to s$.

source.place: Proof, The pushforward to the point: the diagram (a_X,a_C) and its fixed map

proof.text: The finite-coefficient constructible-domain exceptional adjunction in [prop-functor-package], together with the preservation assertion of [thm-sf-preservation-class], supplies the exceptional adjunction on $D^b_{ctf}$ for each separated finite-type map in step 1. Thus all the exceptional admissibility conditions required by [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps] hold for this diagram: $c,b$, the structure maps of $X,s,F,s$, and $f,g,h,i_c,i_b,d_c,d_b$, together with the projections from $X\times_sX$ and $s\times_ss$ used in external duality, are among those maps. The same observation verifies the exceptional admissibility required for the diagonal pair at $s$. Only the constructible exceptional inverse image is used here. Moreover $K'=Ra_{X*}K$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$ by clause (iii) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability], so the pushed correspondence is within the coefficient domain of the trace comparison. Clauses (i) and (v) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] also give $Lc_2^*K,Rc_1^!K\in D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$. These complexes and $K$ are bounded constructible, so the explicit etale-origin assertion in [thm-sf-preservation-class] supplies bounded etale antecedents for them. Choose those antecedents with their comparison isomorphisms. Thus the inputs to the compact-support composition law in step 6 lie in its stated bounded-below etale-origin domain.

source.place: Proof, opening admissibility paragraph; hypotheses for Proper pushforward compatibility and Point normalization

proof.text: Proper coincidence in clause (3) of [prop-functor-package] gives $K'=Ra_{X*}K\cong Ra_{X!}K$ as a sheaf complex on $s$. Put $P=\operatorname{Fib}_s(K')$. The convention [def-trf-coefficient-conventions] identifies $P$ with $R\Gamma_c(X,K)$; it does not identify the sheaf complex $K'$ itself with an ordinary module complex. Apply [lem-trf-global-operator-perfect] to the given admissible $(C,c,u)$, proper $c_2$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Its conclusion is explicitly in the sense of [def-trf-categorical-trace], whose category is $\operatorname{Perf}(A)$, so $P$ is perfect and the endomorphism $T_c(u)$ has its categorical trace. This avoids inferring perfectness from bounded finite cohomology alone. The coevaluation, endomorphism tensor identity, symmetry and evaluation in [def-trf-categorical-trace] are exactly the four arrows defining the ordinary categorical trace of [sk-d-trace], specialized to $\operatorname{Perf}(A)$; thus this is also the trace specified by the current unit.

source.place: Proof, The pushforward to the point: proper coincidence and perfectness

proof.text:
Expand the ordinary half $\gamma:K'\to Ra_{C*}Lc_2^*K$ of [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward]. In this step set $F=La_X^*$, $R=Ra_{X*}$, $L=Lc_2^*$ and $S=Rc_{2*}$; these letters denote functors only in this calculation. Under the adjunction-compatible composition identifications of clause (3) of [fix-prop-adjunctions], its value at $K$ is
$$\gamma_K=RS L(\varepsilon_{a_X,K})\circ R\eta_{c_2,FRK}\circ\eta_{a_X,RK}.$$
Naturality of the unit $\eta_{c_2}:\operatorname{id}\to SL$, applied to $\varepsilon_{a_X,K}:FRK\to K$, gives
$$RS L(\varepsilon_{a_X,K})\circ R\eta_{c_2,FRK}=R\eta_{c_2,K}\circ R\varepsilon_{a_X,K}.$$
The ordinary triangle identity in clause (1) of [fix-prop-adjunctions] says $R\varepsilon_{a_X,K}\circ\eta_{a_X,RK}=1_{RK}$. Hence $\gamma_K=Ra_{X*}(\eta_{c_2,K})$, with target identified by $Ra_{X*}Rc_{2*}\cong Ra_{C*}$.

source.place: Proof, The pushed coefficient map is the global operator: ordinary half gamma

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-proper-exceptional-half-normalization] with $a=a_X$, $d=c_1$, $q=a_C$ and $Y=s$. Properness and separated finite type are established in step 1, and the constructible exceptional adjunctions, finite-Tor outputs and etale-origin inputs in step 3. Identify the exceptional right adjoint of the point identity using the counit specified by that lemma. For the exceptional half $\delta$ of [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward], it gives
$$\delta=j_{X,K}^{-1}\circ Ra_{X!}(\varepsilon_{c_1,K})\circ\alpha_{a_X,c_1,Rc_1^!K}^{-1}\circ j_{C,Rc_1^!K},$$
where $j_X:Ra_{X*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{X!}$ and $j_C:Ra_{C*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{C!}$ are inverse proper coincidence.

source.place: Proof, The pushed coefficient map is the global operator: exceptional half delta and equality of the composites

proof.text:
Use the composition coherence of the proved comparison maps in [fix-prop-coherence], with the proper coincidences and compact-support compositions of [prop-functor-package]. If $\beta:Ra_{X*}Rc_{2*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{C*}$ is ordinary composition and $j_2:Rc_{2*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rc_{2!}$, its proper-composition square is
$$j_C\circ\beta=\alpha_{a_X,c_2}\circ Ra_{X!}(j_2)\circ j_X(Rc_{2*}).$$
These are the canonical comparisons on the finite constructible etale-origin domain checked in step 3. In addition, naturality of the proper-coincidence isomorphism $j_C$, at the morphism $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$, reads
$$j_{C,Rc_1^!K}\circ Ra_{C*}(u)=Ra_{C!}(u)\circ j_{C,Lc_2^*K}.$$
Thus the two comparison identities previously used inline are supplied by an existing coherence node and naturality of the specified natural isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, The pushed coefficient map is the global operator: exceptional half delta and equality of the composites

proof.text:
Put $v=[a_X,a_C]_!u=\delta\circ Ra_{C*}(u)\circ\gamma$ as in [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward]. Substitute the formula for $\gamma$ from step 5, the formula for $\delta$ from step 6, and the two identities of step 7. Naturality of $j_X$ at $\eta_{c_2,K}$ moves $j_X$ to the source, giving
$$j_{X,K}v j_{X,K}^{-1}=Ra_{X!}(\varepsilon_{c_1,K})\circ\alpha_{a_X,c_1}^{-1}\circ Ra_{C!}(u)\circ\alpha_{a_X,c_2}\circ Ra_{X!}(j_2)\circ Ra_{X!}(\eta_{c_2,K}).$$
Applying $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ gives, in order, the unit, $p_{c_2}^{-1}=j_2$, compact-support composition, $u$, inverse composition and counit prescribed in [def-trf-global-operator]. Hence $\operatorname{Fib}_s(v)=T_c(u)$ under the proper-coincidence identification $P=\operatorname{Fib}_s(K')\cong R\Gamma_c(X,K)$ of step 4.

source.place: Proof, The pushed coefficient map is the global operator: exceptional half delta and equality of the composites

proof.text:
Apply [thm-trf-trace-proper-compatibility] to the proper pushforward diagram of step 2, with its exceptional hypotheses verified in step 3. Since its induced fixed map is $a_F$, the result is
$$(a_F)_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)=\operatorname{Tr}_b(v).$$
By step 1 the structure map $a_F$ is separated finite type and by hypothesis is proper; its exceptional admissibility was checked in step 3. Therefore [lem-trf-integration-as-pushforward], at $T=F$ and $\alpha=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$, identifies the left side with $\int_F\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ in $\operatorname{Hom}(A_s,\omega_s)=A$.

The point correspondence $b$ is the diagonal of $s$. Apply [lem-trf-trace-class-diagonal-pairing] with $X=C=s$, coefficient $K'$, and coefficient morphism $v$. The finite-Tor and exceptional hypotheses hold by steps 1 and 3. It gives $\operatorname{Tr}_b(v)=\langle v,1_{K'}\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, $\operatorname{Fib}_s=\Gamma(s,-)$ is an equivalence $D^b_c(s,A)\to D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ by [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence]; hence $K'$ is isomorphic to the coefficient-sheaf version of the perfect complex $P=\operatorname{Fib}_s(K')$ of step 4, and under this isomorphism $v$ corresponds to $\operatorname{Fib}_s(v)$ and $1_{K'}$ to $1_P$. Transport of structure along this isomorphism leaves the supported pairing unchanged. The point normalization [prop-trf-pairing-point-normalization] therefore applies to this pair, whose underlying coefficient complex is the perfect $P$ of step 4. Its right-hand side is the ordinary categorical trace of $1_P\circ\operatorname{Fib}_s(v)$ on $P$. By step 8 this is $\operatorname{tr}_A(T_c(u)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K))$. Substitute into step 9 and reverse the equality to obtain the required formula. No component decomposition, reducedness, smoothness, or Frobenius hypothesis is used.

source.place: Proof, Point normalization and the final equality
